 Pennsylvania Releases Health Insurance Transparency Resources Ahead of Open Enrollment
 By Editor - October 27, 2026 0 4 Facebook Twitter Linkedin Email The Pennsylvania Insurance Department (PID) released two annual reports that help Pennsylvanians better understand health insurance options available in the Commonwealth ahead of Pennie’s Open Enrollment season.
 PID’s Affordable Care Act (ACA) Quality Health Plans (QHP) Summary Report and Transparency in Coverage (TiC) Report provide consumers with information about health plan benefits, coverage, claims, denials, and appeals. Together, the reports can serve as important tools for Pennsylvanians researching health insurance options and making informed decisions about their coverage.
 “Choosing a health insurance plan can be complicated, and Pennsylvanians deserve clear information that helps them understand their options,” said Pennsylvania Insurance Commissioner Michael Humphreys. “These reports give consumers another tool to look at what health plans have to offer, understand how claims and appeals are handled, and ask informed questions as they consider the coverage that works best for them and their families.”
 The Transparency in Coverage Report provides consumers with additional information about how insurers handle claims, claim denials, and appeals. Understanding the claims and appeals process can help consumers know what to do if their insurer denies coverage for treatments, medications, or services.
 A denied claim does not necessarily mark the end of the process. Pennsylvanians who receive a claim denial can first appeal the decision through their insurer’s internal appeals process. Consumers whose claims remain denied following internal review may also be able to request an external independent review through PID.
 By reviewing both reports, consumers can learn more about the benefits and services offered through health plans while also becoming more familiar with their rights and the processes available if they experience issues with their coverage.
 Key takeaways from this year’s TiC Report include:
 The percentage of claims denied increased from 14.8% to 17.35%, still below the national average;
 The percentage of overturned internal appeals dropped from 35.8% to 24.25%;
 New federal reporting requirements gave Pennsylvania its first clear view of pre-service (prior authorization) decisions, revealing a statewide denial rate of 17.5%; and
 Appeals continue to be extremely underutilized—fewer than 1% of denied claims or pre-service requests are appealed—despite significant overturn rates when members do appeal.
 The QHP Summary Report provides consumers with a look at how PID regulates health insurance plans sold in Pennsylvania. All plans sold in the Commonwealth’s commercial market are reviewed for compliance with state and federal laws and regulations, including reviews of rates, required benefits, formularies, mental health parity, and provider network adequacy.
 Qualified Health Plans must meet federal and state coverage requirements, but insurers may offer additional benefits and features. The QHP Summary Report helps make those differences more transparent by examining areas such as preventive and screening services, mental and behavioral health, substance use disorder treatment, maternal and reproductive health, and other health care services. Consumers should review their individual policy or contact their insurer for complete details about their coverage.
